dialogues.speaker: Gorshkov
dialogues.text: The sea breeze feels wonderful today... Which means no rough waves ahead. Just perfect. Think I'll grab a cup of Fire-Water later to celebrate...

dialogues.speaker: Gorshkov
dialogues.text: Me? Just a minor clerk. I mean, my peers have all either made it into the Snezhnograd Veche or the Zapolyarny Palace by now...

dialogues.speaker: Gorshkov
dialogues.text: But working over there is a real drag. There's no way they get to enjoy the sheer peace and leisure I have here...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A toast... just for a nice day?

dialogues.speaker: Gorshkov
dialogues.text: Good weather means we won't see any massive storms out there. And no massive storms means these fishermen can return home safe and sound.

dialogues.speaker: Gorshkov
dialogues.text: Though most of them pride themselves on braving the waves, from the bottom of my heart, I wish they never had to face them at all.

dialogues.speaker: Gorshkov
dialogues.text: Parents get to welcome back their children, and children get to welcome back their parents... Now that is worth raising a glass to today.

dialogues.speaker: Gorshkov
dialogues.text: Goodbye. May you have a pleasant journey.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything of note nearby?

dialogues.speaker: Gorshkov
dialogues.text: Near this spot? Hmm. I'd say Dozorov's pet bear, and precious little else... I mean, looks friendly enough, sure, but s'a bear, you know?
